entries.title: Strict alerts on an unfixed finding and quarantines a fix left undeployed for 7 days
entries.change:
Under security.posture: strict, a distro-acknowledged, network-reachable Medium-or-worse finding with no fix and not on CISA's or the EU's KEV list no longer quarantines. It is AWAITING_FIX, alerted once, and the site stays up. A strict quarantine taken for such a finding before 0.12 is lifted by the first complete scan after the upgrade.
In exchange, a fix that exists must be running within 7 days. The deadline counts from the first scan after the upgrade that finds the fix available and not running. 48 hours before it, one 'Fix deadline' alert names the CVE, the package and the date; at the deadline the project is quarantined until the fix runs (with dangerously_disable_quarantine: true it runs at risk, alerted).
For each strict project, deploy the fixes 'security <project>' lists as fixable within the week: rebuild on current base images, or bump the image tag or digest.
entries.verify: After the first scan, 'security <project>' shows no [QUARANTINE] row for a finding with no fix that is not on full KEV, and no fix-deadline alert arrives for the project once its fixes are deployed.

entries.title: Paranoid quarantines a fixable finding at once
entries.change:
Under security.posture: paranoid, a Medium-or-worse finding (the highest rating any source gives) whose fix exists but is not running used to stay up with the rebuild advice. From 0.12 it is quarantined at once, until the fix runs, and a listing by VulnCheck alone (when that source is on) quarantines like CISA's or the EU's.
Before upgrading, run 'security <project>' for each paranoid project. A finding over the gate with a fixed version will take the site down at the first scan after the upgrade: deploy the fix first (rebuild on current base images, or bump the image tag or digest), or accept the downtime until it is deployed.
entries.verify: After the first scan, 'security <project>' shows status NORMAL, or a quarantine you expected and whose fix is on its way.

entries.title: ENISA's EU KEV list now counts as known exploited; VulnCheck is opt-in
entries.change:
CISA's KEV catalog is no longer the only known-exploited source. ENISA's EU KEV list is fetched beside it, on by default, and a CVE it lists is treated exactly like a CISA listing (full KEV): it quarantines under every posture, overrides suppressions and is refused by the deploy guard. Turn it off with kev.enisa: {enabled: false} in boxmunge.yml (a kev block always needs kev.sources too).
VulnCheck's KEV list is opt-in: set kev.vulncheck.token to a VulnCheck token. A VulnCheck-only listing is alerted urgently but takes a site down only under paranoid. The VulnCheck integration follows VulnCheck's published API documentation and has not yet been run against a live token, so check it after setting one.
A stale source never lifts a quarantine while a CVE it listed is still in the images; --accept-stale-kev is the audited way past.
entries.verify: Run 'security scan', then 'health': the kev-watch check is ok. With a VulnCheck token set, it must not say 'vulncheck_kev not usable'; 'log --component cve-scan' names any fetch error.

entries.title: The nightly CVE scan and container update run as one maintenance unit
entries.change: The separate boxmunge-cve-scan.timer and boxmunge-container-update.timer are replaced by boxmunge-maintenance.timer. It fires at 02:30 with up to 30 minutes of random delay and runs the CVE scan, then the container update, in one unit, so the scan always finishes before the update starts; a failed step does not skip the other. The upgrade disables and removes the two old timers. Move anything outside boxmunge that watched them (monitoring, notes) to the new unit.
entries.verify: As root, 'systemctl list-timers boxmunge-*' lists boxmunge-maintenance.timer and boxmunge-kev-watch.timer, and neither old timer. 'health' passes the timers check.

entries.title: A KEV watch rescans affected projects every 30 minutes
entries.change: boxmunge-kev-watch.timer runs 'security kev-watch' as root every 30 minutes. Each tick refreshes the known-exploited lists and rescans only the projects whose last stored scan holds a newly listed CVE, judging, quarantining and alerting them as the nightly scan would. Its first tick records the lists and rescans nothing. A tick that finds the nightly scan running skips itself; the nightly scan waits for a running tick, at most an hour. The new kev-watch health check warns when the watch stops ticking or a source that is turned on goes stale.
entries.verify: Within an hour of the upgrade, 'health' shows the kev-watch check ok ('the KEV watch is ticking and its sources are fresh').

entries.title: Deploys refuse a release that carries a known-exploited CVE
entries.change:
stage, prod-deploy, promote and rollback now scan every image the release would start and refuse one that carries a CVE on CISA's or the EU's KEV list (under paranoid, VulnCheck's too), whether or not the project is quarantined, and one that brings back a CVE autofix patched in the running release. The refusal names each CVE, package and fixed version; fix it in the repo. --allow-security-regression --reason "<why>" deploys anyway, logged and alerted.
A project that runs such a CVE today (relaxed with a fixable KEV finding, or dangerously_disable_quarantine: true) has its next deploy refused, rollback included, until the release is rebuilt with the fix: plan that rebuild.
On a box that has never fetched the CISA catalog, every deploy is refused until 'security scan' has run once; prod-deploy --accept-stale-kev is the audited exit when no source can be reached.
entries.verify: 'stage <project>' (or prod-deploy) prints 'Deploy guard: no known-exploited CVE in the release's images.' and goes ahead.

entries.title: The first scan after the upgrade re-sends first-scan alerts
entries.change: Stored scan states from before 0.12 do not record which known-exploited lists named each finding, so 0.12 refuses to read them as a prior scan. The first scan after the upgrade treats every project as scanned for the first time and sends its first-scan alerts once more (the fixable, no-fix-yet and known-exploited alerts, and the nightly digest), then rewrites the state. Until a project's state is rewritten, the KEV watch skips it (the nightly scan covers it) and 'security scan --apply-held' cannot apply a breaker hold for it. Quarantine records from before 0.12 are still read: they count as listed by CISA alone. Run 'security scan' after the upgrade to rewrite every state at once.
entries.verify: After 'security scan', 'log --component cve-scan' shows no 'ignoring unreadable prior scan state' warning on the next scan.

entries.title: Autofix patches fixable OS-package CVEs on the box, on by default
entries.change:
Autofix is on by default; set security.autofix: false in a project's manifest to opt out. It patches a fixable OS-package CVE in the running image from the image's own distro repositories (apk or apt images only): a known-exploited one as soon as the scan that found it is over, others that meet the posture's gate in the nightly maintenance run. Each patch is scanned, swapped in and health-checked within 30 minutes, or rolled back. Where the posture takes the site down for the CVE, it may be down while it is patched (agent-help cve, "Autofix", table A).
A patched project runs images that differ from its release, and 'status' shows it as patched. Bring the fix into the repo (bump the base image, or upgrade the packages 'security <project>' lists): the deploy guard refuses a release, rollback included, that brings a patched CVE back. Container updates being off does not stop autofix; only security.autofix: false does.
entries.verify: After the first nightly run, 'status' shows no project as patched that you did not expect, and 'security <project>' lists the patch records of any that is.

entries.title: A new unit, boxmunge-autofix.service, runs the urgent patches
entries.change: boxmunge-autofix.service runs 'security autofix-queue' as root with a 6-hour limit. It has no timer: the nightly scan, the KEV watch and a root 'security scan <project>' start it when they queue a patch, so a long patch never holds up the scans or the container update. It takes each project's own lock only. A run that is killed leaves a journal (state/autofix/<project>.journal), which the next run undoes exactly and alerts; the KEV watch starts that run within half an hour. The nightly patches run inside container-update and send one quiet digest, 'Nightly autofix: ...', one line per project.
entries.verify: As root, 'systemctl cat boxmunge-autofix.service' shows the unit, and 'systemctl list-timers boxmunge-*' lists no autofix timer.

entries.title: Operate actions run as audited jobs: job run, job show and jobs
entries.change:
'boxmunge job run', 'job show' and 'jobs' start and follow operate actions as jobs run by 'boxmunge-jobs.service'; every job is audited. A job (project.deploy, project.backup, project.stage and the other operate actions) runs in the background as deploy, outside your SSH session: at most 4 at once, one at a time per project. It waits up to 2 minutes for its project's lock, then fails busy, naming the holder and the command that retries it. A job cut off by a restart fails worker_lost and is never re-run; the alert names its way out. The direct commands (backup, stage, prod-deploy and the rest) are unchanged.
boxmunge-jobs.path starts the runner whenever a job is queued. The new jobs-runner health check reports an error when that path unit is not active; it names the fix: as the supervisor, sudo systemctl reset-failed boxmunge-jobs.path boxmunge-jobs.service && sudo systemctl start boxmunge-jobs.path.
entries.verify: As the supervisor, 'systemctl status boxmunge-jobs.path' shows the unit active (waiting), and 'boxmunge health' passes the jobs-runner check.

entries.title: An upgrade waits for running jobs and refuses new ones
entries.change: An upgrade waits up to 60 minutes for running jobs; new jobs are refused while it runs. While it waits it logs 'Waiting up to 60 minutes for running jobs to finish'; if jobs still run after that, it installs nothing and stops, and can be run again once they finish. A job refused during an upgrade is refused with unavailable and queues nothing: run the same 'job run' again once the upgrade has finished. A job queued just as an upgrade started stays queued and runs once afterwards, on the new code. Jobs are refused only while an upgrade, or the probation check after one, is actually changing the platform, not for the whole probation. A job still queued 2 hours after it was created is failed with expired and never run; its message names the command that makes the call again.
entries.verify: 'boxmunge jobs --running' lists the jobs an upgrade would wait for; 'boxmunge log --component upgrade' shows any wait.

entries.title: The action audit log is append-only and rotated monthly
entries.change: 'logs/audit.jsonl' is append-only ('chattr +a'); 'boxmunge-audit-rotate.timer' rotates it monthly and keeps 12 months; 'health' reports an error if the attribute is missing, or a warning on a host that cannot set it (some container-based VPS plans). The installer seals the log: deploy cannot truncate, rewrite or delete it; only root can, by lifting the attribute. The fix for the audit-log error is sudo boxmunge-server _audit-seal. On a host that cannot set the attribute, install still completes, records why in upgrade-root/audit-append-unsupported, and deploy can still rewrite the log there.
entries.verify: As root, 'lsattr /opt/boxmunge/logs/audit.jsonl' shows the a attribute, and 'boxmunge health' passes the audit-log check (or warns that this host cannot set it).

entries.title: A git project's boxmunge-scripts/ comes from its repository, and a missing script refuses the deploy
entries.change:
A git project's smoke checks and pre_deploy script needed a boxmunge-scripts/ placed in the project directory by hand, which the deploy shell cannot do; without one, Docker created it empty and owned by root. From 0.12 every checkout (deploy, promote, rollback, abandon, the staged release) of a commit that has boxmunge-scripts/ refreshes the project directory's copy to the commit's, in place; hand-placed scripts are replaced. A commit without one leaves the existing scripts alone, so a rollback to an older commit still finds them. A link inside the committed directory is refused.
A deploy, stage or promote whose manifest names a smoke script, or a relative pre_deploy, that the release lacks is refused before anything starts, naming the file.
Before upgrading, commit boxmunge-scripts/ (regular files) at the top of each git project's repository, and make sure each bundle ships the scripts its manifest names.
entries.verify: 'validate <project>' reports no missing smoke or pre_deploy script, and the next 'prod-deploy <project>' runs its smoke check.

entries.title: validate runs deploy's compose checks; env_files is ignored
entries.change:
'validate <project>' now runs the compose.yml checks a deploy runs (hardening, isolation, the posture rules such as strict's read_only requirement), the missing-script check, and the identity check. A project validate passes is one prod-deploy does not refuse for its configuration; a compose.yml rejection exits 3, as the deploy's does, and a missing compose.yml is an error rather than a warning.
The manifest key env_files never did anything (the overlay always reads the project's project.env). It is gone from the templates, and validate warns about a manifest that still has it; such a manifest keeps validating. Remove the key at your next change to the manifest.
entries.verify: 'validate <project>' for each project prints VALID, or names what the next deploy would refuse.

entries.title: A git project's first release is deployed with prod-deploy
entries.change: 'stage' of a git project that was never deployed is refused, saying to run 'prod-deploy <project>' first: staging is checked against production, and staging.copy_data copies production's data, neither of which exists yet. Stage and promote the releases after it. add-git-project says so, and notes a project.env.example in the repository, which boxmunge does not copy: set the values it lists with 'secrets set <project> KEY=value'.
